newsitem.title: USA: GM, UAW resume talks on parts plant strike.
newsitem.headline: GM, UAW resume talks on parts plant strike.

text.p: Bargainers for the United Auto Workers union and General Motors Corp resumed negotiations at about 0900 EDT/1300 GMT Thursday in an effort to end a strike at a transmission plant that has already idled one GM assembly plant.
GM spokeswoman Darla Park said the two sides talked until about midnight last night.

About 2,700 UAW members walked off the job at midnight Tuesday when talks failed to produce a new contract at the Warren, Mich., plant, which produces automatic transmissions for GM cars and light trucks, including minivans.
The plant also makes wheels and suspension control arms.

The union wants GM to add more employees to reduce overtime burdens and limit outsourcing of work. GM is trying to avoid hiring more employees as it seeks to reduce its overall labor force and improve manufacturing efficiencies.

About 2,700 workers from GM's Buick City assembly plant in Flint, Mich., were told not to report to work today because of a shortage of transmissions. The facility makes Buick LaSabre and Pontiac Bonneville large cars.

A second assembly plant in Orion Township, Mich., which makes the Oldsmobile Aurora and Eighty Eight, Buick Riviera and Bonneville cars, is likely to be idled today, industry sources said. More shutdowns could follow later this week and next week.
Jim Marcum, financial secretary for UAW Local 909, said strikers are not happy about forcing other union members off the job but are standing firm against GM.
"It's an unfortunate by-product," he said. "We don't want other people to be out of work because of us. That's never the union's intention."
